```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Uncertainty in UCDP data is multidimensional. Fatality bounds describe the
reported low, best, and high estimates. Spatial and temporal precision codes
describe how precisely an event is located in place and time. Retrospective
revisions describe changes between releases. These quantities answer different
questions, and `ucdpR` does not collapse them into a single score.

The examples below are fully offline and use small synthetic data.

```{r}
library(ucdpR)

events <- data.frame(
  id = 1:6,
  year = c(2020, 2020, 2020, 2021, 2021, 2021),
  low = c(1, 2, 0, 4, 1, NA),
  best = c(2, 3, 1, 5, 2, NA),
  high = c(4, 5, 2, 8, 4, NA),
  where_prec = c(1, 2, 3, 1, 6, 2),
  date_prec = c(1, 2, 4, 1, 5, 2),
  type_of_violence = c(1, 1, 2, 3, 1, 2)
)
```

## Inventory reported uncertainty

Begin with a descriptive inventory. This reveals incomplete fatality triplets,
the width of complete fatality bounds, and the distribution of precision codes.

```{r}
ucdp_uncertainty(events)
ucdp_uncertainty(events, by = "year")
```

The output keeps fatality, spatial, and temporal dimensions separate. A wider
fatality range is not interchangeable with a less precise location.

## Treat reported bounds as scenarios

`ucdp_scenarios()` creates explicit low, best, and high analytical scenarios.
The bounds are not treated as confidence or credible intervals.

```{r}
scenario_rows <- ucdp_scenarios(events)
head(scenario_rows)

year_scenarios <- ucdp_scenarios(
  events,
  by = "year",
  format = "wide",
  fatality_missing = "remove"
)
year_scenarios
```

Scenario differences can be made explicit:

```{r}
ucdp_compare_scenarios(scenario_rows, by = "id")
```

## Sample only under a stated assumption

`ucdp_sample_fatalities()` is experimental. It samples integer fatalities
between the reported bounds under a user-selected uniform or triangular
distribution. UCDP does not imply either distribution: it is an analytical
assumption that must be reported and defended.

```{r}
complete_events <- events[stats::complete.cases(
  events[c("low", "best", "high")]
), ]

draws <- ucdp_sample_fatalities(
  complete_events,
  n = 5,
  distribution = "triangular",
  seed = 2026,
  id = "id"
)
head(draws)
attr(draws, "ucdp_sampling_spec")
```

Supplying a seed makes the result reproducible without replacing the caller's
existing random-number state. The returned specification records the chosen
distribution and column mapping.

## Run a sensitivity grid

`ucdp_sensitivity()` crosses fatality scenarios with named precision rules. An
analysis function can return one number, a named vector, or a one-row data
frame for each specification.

```{r}
sensitivity <- ucdp_sensitivity(
  complete_events,
  scenarios = c("low", "best", "high"),
  where_prec = list(all = NULL, precise = 1:2),
  date_prec = list(all = NULL, precise = 1:2),
  analysis = function(x) {
    c(events = nrow(x), fatalities = sum(x$.ucdp_fatalities))
  }
)

sensitivity$specifications
sensitivity$results
```

Compare the fatality result with the best estimate within each precision rule:

```{r}
ucdp_compare_scenarios(
  sensitivity,
  value = "fatalities",
  by = c(".where_precision", ".date_precision")
)
```

These comparisons show sensitivity to specified analytical decisions; they do
not estimate the probability that any scenario is true.

## Prepare input for uncertainUCDP

`ucdp_to_uncertainUCDP()` is a narrow adapter. It maps a fatality column and
UCDP type-of-violence codes to the `fatalities` and `tov` arguments used by
`uncertainUCDP`. It validates the mapping but does not fit or reproduce the
external package's statistical model.

```{r}
prepared <- ucdp_to_uncertainUCDP(
  complete_events,
  fatalities = "best",
  type_of_violence = "type_of_violence",
  check_package = FALSE
)
prepared[c(".ucdp_fatalities", ".ucdp_tov")]
```

After installing `uncertainUCDP`, the prepared columns can be passed explicitly
to its simulation function:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
simulated <- uncertainUCDP::runcertainUCDP(
  n = nrow(prepared),
  fatalities = prepared$.ucdp_fatalities,
  tov = prepared$.ucdp_tov
)
```

Consult the `uncertainUCDP` documentation and cite that package when using its
model. Preserve the exact UCDP release, source metadata, and all assumptions in
the research record.
